of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2012) }} '''James Michael Scott''' (born July 16, 1988) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Gigantes de Carolina (men's basketball)|Gigantes de Carolina]] of the Puerto Rican [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].{{cite web|url=https://5aial.com/mike-scott-arrives-in-nancy-as-a-medical-joker/|title=Mike Scott arrives in Nancy as a medical joker|website=5aial.com|access-date=October 17, 2022|archive-date=October 17, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221017013604/https://5aial.com/mike-scott-arrives-in-nancy-as-a-medical-joker/|url-status=dead}} He played college basketball for the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]], before being taken in the second round of the [[2012 NBA draft]], and spending ten seasons in the [[NBA]]. ==High school career== Scott played his high school career at [[Deep Creek High School]] and then prepped for a year at [[Hargrave Military Academy]]. Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Scott was listed as the No. 33 power forward and the No. 115 player in the nation in 2007.{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/55828|title=Mike Scott Recruiting Profile|work=Rivals.com|access-date=October 15, 2013}} ==College career== [[File:VT - UVA 2012 - Mike Scott shooting.jpg|thumb|left|Scott with Virginia in February 2012]] After a solid first three years in which he led the Virginia Cavaliers in [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounding]] as a sophomore and junior, Scott appeared poised for a breakout year in [[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2010–11]]. He began the year averaging 15.9 [[Points per game|points]] and 10.2 rebounds in the team's first ten games. But Scott's season ended early as he suffered an ankle injury and underwent season-ending surgery.{{cite web|first=Steve|last=Yanda|url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/cavaliers-journal/2011/01/mike_scott_to_miss_remainder_o.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220135424/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/cavaliers-journal/2011/01/mike_scott_to_miss_remainder_o.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 20, 2016|title=Mike Scott to miss remainder of season due to ankle injury|work=WashingtonPost.com|date=January 10, 2011|access-date=October 15, 2013}} Due to his injury, Scott was granted a [[Redshirt (college sports)|medical redshirt]] and a fifth year of eligibility. He was one of the top players in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) in [[2011–12 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|2011–12]], averaging 18.0 points and 8.3 rebounds per game and led the ACC in [[field goal percentage]] at .563. He led the Cavaliers to a 22–10 record and their first [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA tournament]] berth in five years, but lost to [[2011–12 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] in the round of 64. Scott received conference recognition as the second-leading vote getter for the All-ACC team and national recognition as an [[2012 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] by the [[Sporting News]] (third team) and the [[Associated Press]] (Honorable Mention). Scott finished his Virginia career with 1,538 points and is the third leading rebounder in Cavalier history with 944.{{cite web|url=http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/scott_mike00.html|title=Mike Scott Bio|work=VirginiaSports.com|access-date=October 15, 2013|archive-date=April 25, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130425051528/http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/scott_mike00.html|url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== ===Atlanta Hawks (2012–2017)=== [[File:1 mike scott 2015.jpg|thumb|right|Scott with the Hawks in April 2015]] On June 28, 2012, Scott was selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the 43rd overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-select-john-jenkins-and-mike-scott-2012-nba-draft-0|title=HAWKS SELECT JOHN JENKINS AND MIKE SCOTT IN 2012 NBA DRAFT|work=NBA.com|date=June 28, 2012|access-date=December 7, 2016}} On September 6, 2012, he signed with the Hawks.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-second-round-draft-pick-mike-scott|title=ATLANTA HAWKS SIGN SECOND ROUND DRAFT PICK MIKE SCOTT|work=NBA.com|date=September 6, 2012|access-date=September 6, 2012}} On December 1, 2012, he was assigned to the [[Northern Arizona Suns|Bakersfield Jam]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-assign-jenkins-and-scott-bakersfield-jam|title=HAWKS ASSIGN JENKINS AND SCOTT TO BAKERSFIELD JAM|work=NBA.com|date=December 1, 2012|access-date=December 1, 2012}} He was recalled by the Hawks on December 11,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-recall-mike-scott-bakersfield-jam|title=HAWKS RECALL SCOTT FROM BAKERSFIELD JAM|work=NBA.com|date=December 11, 2012|access-date=December 11, 2012}} reassigned on March 1,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/atlanta_hawks_reassign_mike_scott_bakersfield_jam_2013_03_01.html |title=Atlanta Hawks Re-Assign Mike Scott to NBA D-League 30 points in a 107–98 win over the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|first=George|last=Henry|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140222/NYKATL/gameinfo.html|title=Scott scores career high 30 as Hawks beat 23, 2015|url-status=dead}} He became a primary scoring option off the bench for the Hawks in 2013–14,{{cite web|first=Adam|last=McGee|url=http://hoopshabit.com/2014/06/19/atlanta-hawks-mike-scott-2013-14-season-review/|title=Atlanta Hawks: Mike Scott 2013-14 Season Review|work=HoopsHabit.com|date=June 19, 2014|access-date=June 19, 2014}} averaging a career-high 9.6 points per game on the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/scottmi01/gamelog/2014/|title=Mike Scott 2013-14 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 7, 2016}} On August 26, 2014, Scott re-signed with the Hawks.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-re-sign-mike-scott|title=Hawks Re-Sign Mike Scott|work=NBA.com|date=August 26, 2014|access-date=August 26, 2014}} On March 14, 2015, he was ruled out indefinitely after suffering a left toe injury against the [[Denver Nuggets]] three days earlier.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/03/14/hawks-mike-scott-release/|title=Hawks: Forward Mike Scott has fractured toe|work=NBA.com|date=March 14, 2015|access-date=March 14, 2015}} He missed 11 games with the injury, returning to action on April 4 against the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|first=Charles|last=Odum|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150404/BKNATL/gameinfo.html|title=Millsap hurt as Hawks rout Nets, tie team mark with 57th win|work=NBA.com|date=April 4, 2015|access-date=April 4, 2015}} After getting arrested in July 2015 for drug possession, many believed Scott would be cut by the Hawks.{{cite web|last=Rowland|first=Brad|url=https://www.peachtreehoops.com/2016/2/4/10914908/mike-scott-atlanta-hawks-arrest-2015-2016-season|title=Mike Scott enjoying nice season following off-court turmoil|work=peachtreehoops.com|date=February 4, 2016|access-date=December 19, 2017}} With his legal process still pending, Atlanta chose to keep Scott on the roster for the 2015–16 season. He shot a career-best 3-point percentage during the year, reaching as high as 40.9%. On October 31, 2016, Scott was ruled out for four weeks while undergoing a series of non-surgical procedures for his left knee soreness.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/mike-scott-miss-4-weeks-knee-procedures|title=Mike Scott To Miss 4 Weeks For Knee Procedures|work=NBA.com|date=October 31, 2016|access-date=October 31, 2016}} During the 2016–17 season, he had three assignments to the [[NBA Development League]], two with the [[Long Island Nets]] and one with the [[Delaware 87ers]].{{cite web|url=http://gleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 19, 2017}} On February 23, 2017, Scott was traded, along with the rights to [[Cenk Akyol]] and cash considerations, to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for a top-55 protected 2017 second-round pick.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/phoenix-suns-acquire-mike-scott-atlanta|title=Phoenix Suns Acquire Mike Scott From Atlanta|work=NBA.com|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 23, 2017}} He was waived by the Suns the following day.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-price-waive-scott-sullinger|title=Suns Sign Price, Waive Scott, Sullinger|work=NBA.com|date=February 24, 2017|access-date=February 24, 2017}} ===Washington Wizards (2017–2018)=== On July 9, 2017, Scott signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2017/07/09/wizards-sign-mike-scott|title=Wizards Sign Mike Scott|work=MonumentalSportsnetwork.com|date=July 9, 2017|access-date=July 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190727024439/https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2017/07/09/wizards-sign-mike-scott|archive-date=July 27, 2019|url-status=dead}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2018–2019)=== On July 9, 2018, Scott signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-la-clippers-sign-forward-mike-scott|title=Press Release: L.A. Clippers Sign Forward Mike Scott|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2018|access-date=July 9, 2018}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2019–2021)=== On February 6, 2019, Scott was traded, along with [[Tobias Harris]] and [[Boban Marjanović]], to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for [[Wilson Chandler]], [[Mike Muscala]], [[Landry Shamet]] and a number of future draft picks.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/harris-marjanovic-and-scott-acquired-la-clippers|title=Harris, Marjanović, and Scott Acquired From LA Clippers|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2019|access-date=February 6, 2019}} On July 11, Scott re-signed with the 76ers for two years on a deal worth $9.8 million.{{cite web |title=Team Re-Signs Scott |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/team-re-signs-scott |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 18, 2021 |date=July 11, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Delgado |first1=Dane |title=Report: Sixers to re-sign Mike Scott to two-year deal |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2019/06/30/report-sixers-to-re-sign-mike-scott-to-two-year-deal/ |website=NBC Sports |access-date=November 18, 2021 |date=July 1, 2019}} ===SLUC Nancy Basket (2022–2023)=== On October 16, 2022, Scott signed with [[SLUC Nancy Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite web |title=Former Sixers forward Mike Scott to sign with SLUC team in France |url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/2022/10/16/former-sixers-forward-mike-scott-to-sign-with-sluc-team-in-france/ |access-date=January 11, 2023 |website=USA Today|date=October 16, 2022 }} ===Gigantes de Carolina (2023)=== On May 30, 2023, Scott signed with the [[Gigantes de Carolina (men's basketball)|Gigantes de Carolina]] in Puerto Rico and helped them secure Carolina first Championship in the BSN. He was named Finals MVP for his performance. ===ASVEL (2023–2024)=== On July 31, 2023, Scott signed with [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]].{{cite web|title=Mike Scott nouvelle recrue!|url=https://ldlcasvel.com/mike-scott-nouvelle-recrue/|website=LDLCAsvel.com|date=July 31, 2023|access-date=August 4, 2023|language=fr}} ===Return to Gigantes (2024)=== On March 23, 2024, Scott re-signed with the [[Gigantes de Carolina (men's basketball)|Gigantes de Carolina]].{{cite tweet|author=La Guerra del BSN|title=#BSNPR El delantero Mike Scott regresará a reforzar a los Gigantes de Carolina en la temporada 2024 según informó el apoderado Héctor Horta. and his brother, Antonn, were arrested for drug charges after 35.2 grams of [[marijuana]] and 10.9 grams of [[MDMA]] were found in a [[SUV]] driven by Antonn. The vehicle originally had been stopped for following too closely in [[Banks County, Georgia]] on [[Interstate 85]] northeast of [[Atlanta]]; the vehicle failed to yield for about two miles, with speeds reaching 98 mph, before it finally pulled over.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/07/30/hawks-forward-mike-scott-arrested-on-drug-charges-ap.ap/index.html|title=Hawks' Mike Scott arrested on drug charges|work=NBA.com|date=July 30, 2015|access-date=July 30, 2015}} Scott was facing a possible 25-year prison sentence for his drug charges.{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Vivlamore|url=http://www.ajc.com/sports/basketball/atlanta-hawks-mike-scott-faces-years-drug-charges/SEQqlTp8NNDvKrwWQ1T1yI/|title=Atlanta Hawks' Mike Scott faces up to 25 years
